name: Central Georgetown
tagline: Stabroek Market, the cathedral and the canals
description: The commercial heart of the city around Stabroek Market with its iron clock tower, and St George's Cathedral a few streets away, one of the tallest wooden buildings in the world. Dutch drainage canals still run down the middle of several avenues.
bestFor: Anyone who needs banks, ministries and the markets daily
pros: Stabroek Market and the wooden cathedral
Minibuses to the whole coast from here
cons: Requires real caution, especially after dark

name: Queenstown and Bel Air
tagline: The residential streets the oil money moved into
description: The quieter residential districts east and south of the centre, with older wooden houses, embassies and the newer apartment blocks that the oil boom has brought. Rents here have risen faster than anywhere else in the country since 2019.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting security and newer housing
pros: Newest apartment stock and best internet
cons: Rents have risen sharply with the oil sector
A car or regular taxis are needed

name: Kitty and Campbellville
tagline: Ordinary Georgetown, east of the centre
description: Working residential districts east of the city centre, denser and considerably cheaper than Bel Air, with their own markets and a seawall along the northern edge where the whole city walks in the evening. This is where most Georgetowners actually live.
bestFor: Long stays at local prices with the seawall nearby
pros: Much cheaper than the embassy districts
The seawall promenade in the evening

name: Ogle and the East Coast
tagline: Out towards the airstrip and the coast road
description: The corridor southeast of the city towards Ogle aerodrome, where the light aircraft to Kaieteur and the interior leave from, with newer development along the coast road and the sea defences beyond. It is where much of the oil sector's support base has settled.
bestFor: Anyone flying into the interior regularly or working with the energy sector
pros: Away from the congestion of the centre
cons: Character is functional rather than attractive
